title: Deep research agents
summary: A long-horizon agent plans, searches many sources in parallel, reads them and writes a cited report. It can take tens of minutes and many times the tokens of a chat, so value per task and verification decide whether it pays.
useIf: The question is open-ended and breadth-first, the report is worth real money or time, and you can check citations.
avoidIf: A single retrieval-augmented answer is enough, latency must be seconds, or no one will verify the sources.

explain.md: A **deep research agent** is an orchestrator-workers pattern. A lead agent plans, workers search and read in parallel, and the lead synthesizes a report with citations. Anthropic's write-up of its multi-agent research system reports about 4x the tokens of a chat for an agent and about 15x for multi-agent, token usage explaining 80% of BrowseComp variance (95% with tool calls and model choice), a 90.2% gain over single-agent Opus 4 on its internal eval and research time cut by up to 90% by parallel subagents and tools. These are vendor-reported figures on 2025 models, and the value must justify the cost [[r47]].

explain.title: Deep research shape
explain.alt: A question goes to a lead agent that plans and fans out to parallel search workers. Workers return findings, the lead synthesizes a cited draft, and a verifier checks claims against sources before the report is released.
explain.src:
flowchart TB
  Q[Question] --> L[Lead: plan]
  L --> W1[Worker: search and read]
  L --> W2[Worker: search and read]
  L --> W3[Worker: search and read]
  W1 --> S[Synthesize with citations]
  W2 --> S
  W3 --> S
  S --> V[Verify claims]
  V --> R[Report]

explain.md: **Vendor models and their churn.** OpenAI's `o3-deep-research` and `o4-mini-deep-research` run through the Responses API and need at least one data source: web search, remote MCP or file search. Its deprecation notice lists 2026-07-23 as the shutdown date with `gpt-5.6-sol` as the replacement, and the docs say changing the model ID alone is not a complete migration. That date had passed by 2026-10-13 [[r37]]. The Foundry Deep Research tool is deprecated. Azure cites 2026-11-19 for `o3-deep-research`, which differs from OpenAI's date, probably because the platforms keep separate schedules (an inference). The old tool needed `2025-05-15-preview`, West US or Norway East and Grounding with Bing, so data leaves the Azure compliance boundary [[r38]].

**Operating facts** for OpenAI deep research: run in background mode because tasks can take tens of minutes. Background mode keeps data for about 10 minutes, so it conflicts with ZDR [[r37]] [[tr7]]. A remote MCP server must expose `search` and `fetch` tools and `require_approval` must be `never`. File search accepts a current maximum of two vector stores. The API has no clarification or prompt-rewriting step, so send a fully formed prompt [[r37]].

explain.title: Verify, do not trust the polish
explain.md: A well-formatted report with citations can still cite a source that does not say what the report claims. Check claim against source, sample for fabricated URLs and cap spend per task.

whereToUse: Market, legal or scientific literature scans where breadth matters and a human reviews the output
Reporting across large bodies of internal documents, through file search or an MCP search interface
Due diligence and competitor briefs that justify minutes of runtime and a larger token bill
Any task where parallel exploration beats a single linear search

use: The task is open-ended, breadth-first and valuable enough for 4x to 15x token use
You can verify claims against sources and sample for errors
A background, asynchronous workflow is acceptable
avoid: Simple lookups that a single retrieval call answers
Interactive paths with a seconds-level latency budget
Sensitive data paths where the tool sends queries or content outside your compliance boundary
flips: Sources are internal: build on MCP or file search so data stays inside your boundary
Source is the public web: a vendor model or a latest GPT with web search is reasonable, after you check retirement dates
Writes are coupled (the output is one artifact): keep one writer and use workers only for reading

pitfalls.symptom: Report cites a source that does not support the claim
pitfalls.cause: Synthesis blended sources or the model invented a link
pitfalls.fix: Verify claim-level against fetched text, keep source spans and block uncited claims.

pitfalls.symptom: Costs per task are far above a normal chat
pitfalls.cause: Parallel workers multiply tokens, about 15x for multi-agent in Anthropic's data
pitfalls.fix: Gate by task value, cap budget and worker count and monitor tokens per run.

pitfalls.symptom: A migration breaks after swapping the model ID
pitfalls.cause: Tools and configuration differ, so changing the ID alone is not a complete migration
pitfalls.fix: Re-test tools, data sources and prompts on the replacement and watch the retirement dates.

scenarios.title: Weekly public-web competitor brief
scenarios.situation: An analyst team wants a weekly brief from public sources on five competitors. Nothing confidential is sent out. A person reviews the result.
unknowns: Which model does the platform offer after retirements?
scenarios.question: What do you choose?

options.name: Adopt the Foundry Deep Research tool
options.why: It is deprecated and needs Grounding with Bing, so data leaves the Azure compliance boundary.
options.tradeoff: Only relevant for an existing system you are migrating off.

options.name: A current GPT with web search in a planned research loop, citations required and spend capped
options.why: It follows OpenAI's migration direction, and a human reviews the cited output.
options.tradeoff: You build and evaluate the loop and re-test whenever models change.

options.name: Keep `o3-deep-research` on Azure until its retirement
options.tradeoff: Azure cites 2026-11-19 retirement, so you inherit a deadline.

flips.if: The brief includes confidential internal text
flips.then: Keep queries and content inside your boundary and avoid public-web grounding for that part.
Use a single agent with web search.

scenarios.takeaway: Check retirement dates before building on a vendor research model.

scenarios.title: Research across internal documents
scenarios.situation: Lawyers want a synthesis across thousands of internal documents. Data must not leave the compliance boundary and each person may see only their permitted files.
unknowns: Can retrieval run as the user?
scenarios.question: Which architecture fits?

options.name: Build workers over permission-aware search through MCP or file search, with citation checks
options.why: Sources and permissions stay under your control and data stays in your boundary.

options.name: Foundry Deep Research tool with Bing grounding
options.why: Bing grounding sends data outside the Azure compliance boundary, and the tool is deprecated.
options.tradeoff: Fits only public research with no confidential content.

options.name: A vendor deep research model with file search
options.why: Fast start with documents in vector stores.
options.tradeoff: At most two vector stores and limited permission control, so check per-user access.

flips.then: A vendor model with file search may be enough.

scenarios.takeaway: Internal sources favour building on your own search and MCP.

scenarios.title: Deep research for every support ticket
scenarios.situation: A product manager proposes running deep research on every incoming support ticket to improve answers. Tickets are short, high volume and mostly routine.
unknowns: What share of tickets are truly open-ended?
What is the value of a better answer?
scenarios.question: How do you apply deep research?

options.name: Run it on every ticket for maximum quality
options.why: Multi-agent runs use about 15x the tokens of chat in Anthropic's data and take minutes, which breaks the latency and cost profile.
options.tradeoff: Right for rare, high-value, open-ended cases.

options.name: Use RAG by default and escalate rare complex tickets to deep research asynchronously
options.why: It matches cost and latency to value: routine tickets stay cheap and fast.
options.tradeoff: You need a routing rule and a queue for escalations.

options.name: Use a single agent with web search for all tickets
options.why: Cheaper than multi-agent and more flexible than plain RAG.
options.tradeoff: Still slower and costlier than RAG for routine tickets.

flips.if: Ticket value is high, for example enterprise escalations
flips.then: Deep research on those becomes justified.
Re-run the cost model and consider a cheaper research loop.

scenarios.takeaway: Pay for deep research only where value per task covers the multiplier.

quiz.q: A chat answer uses 10,000 tokens. Using Anthropic's reported multi-agent multiplier of about 15x, roughly how many tokens does a multi-agent research run use?
quiz.explain: 10,000 x 15 is about 150,000 tokens. The 15x figure is vendor-reported on 2025 models, so measure your own runs.

quiz.q: Which are true for OpenAI's deep research models in the Responses API?
options: At least one data source is required
A remote MCP server must expose `search` and `fetch`
Background mode is compatible with ZDR
The API adds a clarification step automatically
quiz.explain: A data source is required and a remote MCP server needs `search` and `fetch` tools. Background mode keeps data for about 10 minutes, which conflicts with ZDR, and the API has no clarification or rewriting step.

quiz.q: Why is the Foundry Deep Research tool a poor fit for confidential data?
options: It cannot cite sources, so reports are unverifiable by design
It needs Bing grounding, so data leaves the Azure boundary
It only runs offline against a local index of documents
It requires a customer-managed key before it will start
quiz.explain: The old tool needed Grounding with Bing, which sends data outside the Azure compliance boundary. It can cite sources, it is not offline and it does not require CMK.

flashcards.front: How much more do agents and multi-agent systems cost in tokens, per Anthropic?
flashcards.back: About 4x for an agent and about 15x for multi-agent versus chat, on its own traffic. Vendor-reported, so measure your own.

flashcards.front: What must a remote MCP server provide for OpenAI deep research?
flashcards.back: A `search` tool and a `fetch` tool, with `require_approval` set to `never`.

flashcards.front: Why is deep research in background mode awkward under ZDR?
flashcards.back: Background mode retains response data for about 10 minutes so polling works, which conflicts with zero data retention.
